correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the stated finite n,m, Metzler Hurwitz A, nonnegative b_l,c, positive a_l, independent symmetric rate-gamma two-state forcing, independent Gaussian thermal noise and reachability assumptions. Stable convolution exists; e^{At}>=0 follows by shifting Metzler A and exponentiating; each h_l(t)=c^T e^{At}b_l is exponentially decaying nonnegative and positive on an interval if reached. For sorted input times t1<t2<t3<t4, Markov conditioning yields E sigma1sigma2sigma3sigma4=e^{-2 gamma[(t2-t1)+(t4-t3)]}; subtracting three pairing contractions yields cum4=-2e^{-2 gamma[(t3-t1)+(t4-t2)]}. Fubini and 24 ordered time chambers give the source exact -48 fourfold response integral with exp[-2 gamma(u+2v+w)], independent sources summing in a_l^4 and independent Gaussian contribution vanishing. Positive integrand is strictly positive on a nonzero-volume region. All gamma derivatives follow by positive Laplace transform and dominated differentiation, strict even for j>0. At gamma->0 the four-fold ordered integration equals 1/24 of the fourth power of the response integral, so -48/24=-2. At infinity scaling three gaps U,V,W by 1/gamma gives gap integral 1/16 and coefficient -48/16=-3 times integral h^4; the variance covariance kernel gives gamma Var->sum a_l^2 integral h_l^2 and the normalized -3/gamma law only when Gaussian thermal variance vanishes. Matching stationary OU with decay 2gamma and variance 1 proves equality of all two-time covariance matrices, not of fourth moments. An independently written symbolic 16-mode exponential convolution rederived the exact two-site variance and K4 rational functions, gamma=1 values, -1/320 fast coefficient, -2/81 frozen limit, and positive 10825/918528 signed-probe counterexample. Tests corroborate examples; general theorem is the analytic proof, not numerical extrapolation.
residual_risks: Formal machine checking was not performed; the proof uses standard Fubini, dominated convergence and Metzler-semigroup positivity.
No uniform-in-network-size bound, arbitrary signed-probe sign or nonzero-thermal excess kurtosis law is proved; the signed example explicitly rules out the unrestricted sign.

value.rationale: The natural physically motivated question is whether stationary displacement statistics of a cooperative overdamped harmonic network can distinguish symmetric bounded active telegraph noise from Gaussian colored forcing despite exactly identical full two-time position covariance. The all-site, all finite stable Metzler network sign obstruction, strict rate ordering, quantitative sharp gamma^-3 coefficient and gamma^-1 standardized decay are structural, testable statements about a natural positivity cone, rather than an isolated parameter substitution. The signed-probe positive counterexample identifies why the cone hypothesis is necessary. The result does not claim original Gaussian covariance matching, original one-pole telegraph kurtosis, or a thermodynamic-limit theorem.
residual_risks: The general positive-filter theorem may ultimately be regarded as a corollary of a more general prior cumulant-transfer formula; exact priority remains qualified.
Physical measurement of high cumulants depends on noise and finite sampling, not analyzed; no large-network uniformity.

final_claim: For every finite stable Metzler network with independent symmetric telegraph forcing, every nonnegative reachable linear readout has strictly negative stationary fourth cumulant at each gamma>0. The magnitude is strictly completely monotone in gamma, tends to -2 sum a_l^4 (integral h_l)^4 as gamma->0 and has gamma^3 K4->-3 sum a_l^4 integral h_l^4 as gamma->infinity; matched Gaussian OU forcing has the same all-lag covariance but zero K4. With no thermal readout variance the excess kurtosis decays as -3/gamma times the displayed response ratio. Signed readouts can have positive K4.
